text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu unveils final-status proposal.
- Six-Day War dead remembered.
- Israel gets $600 million helicopter contract from Poland.
- Solel Boneh oversubscription highest since Tel Aviv Stock Exchange crash in 1993.
- Study: Internet phones to cost Bezeq $31 million by 2001.
- Trade deficit of food industry to rise 35 percent.
- Workers to vie for El Al ownership.
GLOBES
- Orbit Semiconductor decides finally to invest $230 million in Eilat.
- Prime minister's director-general Avigdor Lieberman tells Netanyahu of decision to quit his job at end of July.
- Electricity rates increase by 2.64 percent.
- Dollar soars to record 3.413 shekels.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu presents "Allon-Plus" final status proposal in security cabinet. Commentator Ze'ev Schiff: It's a bid to appear as the heir to the Rabin-Allon legacy.
- Warning strike by teachers association; lessons to start at 10 a.m.
- New Labour leader Ehud Barak about to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat; Yossi Beilin will propose forming a shadow government in Labour.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Hizbollah guerrillas in Lebanon try to flood the state of Israel with drugs, say Western intelligence sources.
- Attorney general in letter to Netanyahu: Israel should consider barring Palestinian justice minister from entry over his land-dealer statements.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu offers "Allon-Plus plan" but Arafat says there's nothing to talk about.
